sources.title: Yaquis - Etnografía - Atlas de los Pueblos Indígenas de México. INPI
sources.annotation: Retained INPI government reading lead for Sonora. Direct retrieval returned 502 during both saved review and this follow-up. Search-index material was not used as a completed original-page review.
sources.countReason: Original page content not successfully inspected.
sources.accessNotes: Automated 502 is not evidence of a reader paywall or of missing community records.

sources.title: Culture - Pascua Yaqui Tribe
sources.annotation: A short Pascua Yaqui Tribe cultural orientation. Its public introductory text was read, but detailed ceremonial descriptions and location links are outside this guide’s synthesis. It does not describe Texas Band institutions.
sources.contentReviewScope: Public Culture page main text, including opening orientation; no linked ceremony/location pages or images inspected.
sources.countReason: Short orientation, retained as supporting context.

sources.title: Departments - Pascua Yaqui Tribe
sources.annotation: Retained official Pascua Yaqui departmental navigation lead. Linked program pages are separate works below; this index is not counted as substantive evidence.
sources.countReason: Navigation lead only; no substantive original content review recorded.

sources.title: Who we are — Texas Band of Yaqui Indians
sources.annotation: The publisher describes its Yoeme family history through displacement from Sonora and continuing community relationships. Read with its longer About account as one institutional self-account. Its legal-authority and recognition assertions are not independently verified here.
sources.contentReviewScope: Complete readable main body, naming and relationship statements; web lines 17–35. The longer About route was also read and is excluded as a second work.

inspectedSubresources.title: Longer About account
inspectedSubresources.scope: Complete readable body, lines20–84; same institutional account, not an independent additional work.

sources.accessNotes: Public readable text. Publication/revision date unstated. No images, certificates, genealogy or private records inspected.

sources.title: About Us — longer Texas Band institutional account
sources.annotation: A longer account of the publisher’s Presidio/Fort Davis migration history and relationship to other Yaqui communities. Retained as an alternate reading route to the same institutional account, not additional corroboration. A paragraph linking an 1864 arrangement with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo was not adopted.
sources.contentReviewScope: Complete readable substantive body, lines 20–84. No underlying census, genealogy, certificates or reservation documents inspected.
sources.countReason: Same institutional self-account as Source 4; excluded to avoid duplicate counting.

sources.title: Senate Resolution 989, enrolled text, 84th Texas Legislature
sources.annotation: Adopted May 27, 2015. The operative clauses honor Texas Band members and request a commemorative copy. Historical recitals are not an independent archival audit. This short instrument does not resolve the wider status questions in this review.
sources.contentReviewScope: Entire enrolled resolution and adoption certification, lines 4–61.
sources.countReason: Short commemorative primary record; supporting, not a substantial historical study.

sources.title: Yaqui — background sheet
sources.publisher: Arizona State Museum, University of Arizona
sources.annotation: A brief museum orientation locating the homeland in Sonora’s Yaqui River valley and noting communities in Texas, Arizona and California. Its generalized recognition wording should be read with the specific 1978 statute below. Population totals, war chronology and ceremonial narratives are not adopted here.
sources.contentReviewScope: All searchable text of the two-page PDF, lines 0–34; no separate visual image/map review.
sources.countReason: Brief orientation rather than a substantive people-level history.
sources.accessNotes: Public PDF. Document date unstated; current figures and the linked website’s services were not checked.

sources.title: Studies of the Yaqui Indians of Sonora, Mexico — selected introduction
sources.publisher: W. C. Holden and colleagues; Texas Technological College
sources.annotation: One 1936 expedition account, inspected only in its introduction and front matter. Holden describes intermediaries, translation and the party’s 1934 Sonora fieldwork. This is evidence about that research encounter, not proof of Texas settlement; modern hosting does not imply endorsement.
sources.contentReviewScope: Title/imprint, acknowledgments and contents; printed pp. 7–8 and opening p. 9 through the visits-to-Vícam/Tórin passage (PDF pp. 9–11). Remaining chapters, illustrations, anthropometric, medical and ceremonial material were not selected.
sources.accessNotes: Public reading copy linked by the Pascua Yaqui Tribal Library. No reuse license established; link-only. Not a full-book content check.

sources.title: Public Law 95-375, as enacted September 18, 1978
sources.annotation: The two-page enactment concerns the named Pascua Yaqui association/Tribe in Arizona, including eligibility for federal services, trust-land provisions, governing documents and membership. It is a dated primary record; later amendments and current consolidated law were not reviewed.
sources.contentReviewScope: Complete two-page statute,92 Stat.712–713, including sections 1–3 and legislative-history footer.
sources.accessNotes: Official publicPDF. Used for historical scope, not current enrollment criteria, jurisdiction or legal advice.

sources.title: Teacher Language Institute — program and educator accounts
sources.annotation: The Tribe describes teacher preparation, language instruction and family/curriculum goals, with educator perspectives. These are the publisher’s stated aims and individual accounts; certification totals, outcomes and a Texas program are not established.
sources.contentReviewScope: TLI program information, goals/core values and Graciela Garcia/Celia Gonzales accounts, web lines 173–211. Other linked programs and images not inspected.
sources.accessNotes: Undated public program page; no current participant count or measured outcomes used.

sources.title: Dr. Fernando Escalante Tribal Library — mission and services
sources.annotation: A community-published account of literacy, Hiaki collections, family programming and technology access. Linked books are reading routes, not additional completed source checks. Services are described as posted, without checking enrollment or access requirements.
sources.contentReviewScope: Mission and department-services sections, web lines 163–193; catalogue/database links noted but not used. Hours, contact records and images not used.
sources.accessNotes: Public text. Individual digital services and library-card/account requirements were not tested.

sources.title: Diccionario yaqui de bolsillo: Jiak noki–español / Español–Jiak noki
sources.publisher: Crescencio Buitimea Valenzuela, Zarina Estrada Fernández, Aarón Grageda Bustamante, Manuel Carlos Silva Encinas; Universidad de Sonora
sources.annotation: A 2016 bilingual dictionary whose acknowledgments and teacher-written foreword describe collaboration with Yaqui-speaking educators and educational purposes. Only front matter and the foreword were inspected; no comprehensive vocabulary or dialect-coverage review is claimed.
sources.contentReviewScope: Title/copyright (printed pp. 5–6), acknowledgments (p. 7) and Prólogo (pp. 9–12), corresponding PDF pp. 7–9 and 11–14 of the 239-page hosted copy. The ResearchGate cover sheet is not counted as another edition/work.
sources.accessNotes: Public PDF supplied through the Tribal Library. Copyright statements retained; no image/text reproduction or reuse license claimed. Hosting is not blanket endorsement of every passage.

remainingLimits: Substantive Texas migration history still rests mainly on one institutional account; primary records and distinct community perspectives remain needed.
No comprehensive Sonora community-history, land/water-history or language review has been completed.
The 2015 resolution’s broader legal effects, the older About page’s reservation/treaty assertion and related certificates remain unassessed; no federal-status equivalence is inferred.
The 1936 book and 2016 dictionary were inspected only in the selected front matter/introduction, not in full.
Program descriptions establish stated activities/aims, not outcomes, speaker counts or universal practice.
The INPI original page remained unavailable to direct retrieval; indexed search text was not counted.
Authentic profile photography is still pending; neutral decorative treatment is not ethnographic art.
No community review or endorsement is recorded.
visualReview: Coordinated neutral card/page treatment; authentic imagery pending; no substituted community object or generated documentary content.
